title: Reject unrecognised CLI options
lead: Each CLI command accepts only the options it uses and fails before reading input or writing output when given anything else, so a mistyped protection option cannot silently produce an unprotected manifest.
findings_note: Obfuscator.Cli/ObfuscatorCliProgram.cs ParseOptions accepts any --token; a typo like --gpg-recipent or --pasphrase-file is silently ignored and the manifest is written unprotected
boundary: **Not in this slice:** library (Obfuscator/) option changes; moving --deterministic-key off the command line (ob-08); per-command --help output.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: `ParseOptions` stores every `--token` it sees and each command reads only the keys it knows. A typo such as `--gpg-recipent` or `--pasphrase-file`, or an option that belongs to another command (for example `--gpg-recipient` on `deobfuscate`), is dropped without a warning. For `obfuscate`, that writes the manifest without the protection the user asked for.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: Obfuscator.Cli/ObfuscatorCliProgram.cs; Obfuscator.Tests/ObfuscatorTests.cs; Obfuscator.Cli/README.md; README.md if it lists CLI options.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `obfuscate` with a mistyped option (`--gpg-recipent x`, `--pasphrase-file f`) exits 1, names the option and the command, and writes no output or manifest.
- `--pasphrase=secret-value` is rejected as unknown and the error does not contain the value after `=`.
- An option valid for another command is rejected: `--gpg-recipient` on `deobfuscate`, `--seed` on `generate`.
- Every option listed in the usage text for each command is still accepted (no regression), including case-insensitive spelling as today.
- The existing inline `--passphrase` rejection message and no-echo tests still pass.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Define the accepted option set per command (value options and flag options) and have `ParseOptions` take that set. An unknown option throws `Unknown option '<name>' for '<command>'.`, where `<name>` is the token up to any `=`, so a value written inline is never echoed. Keep the inline `--passphrase` check ahead of the unknown-option check so its guidance message is unchanged. Keep the usage text and the CLI README consistent with the accepted sets and state that unknown options are rejected.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Run the focused CLI tests, then `dotnet test Obfuscator.slnx` and `scripts/test-local.sh`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Do not change library (`Obfuscator/`) behaviour or option semantics; this slice only changes CLI argument parsing and its docs.
